body.en: The modulus function, composite functions, inverses, and domain and range.

\( |x|=c \) gives \( x=\pm c \). A composite \( fg(x)=f(g(x)) \) is applied inside-out. The inverse \( f^{-1} \) reverses \( f \); swap \( x \) and \( y \) and solve. The range of \( f \) is the domain of \( f^{-1} \).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Functions: Modulus & Inverse

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions: Modulus & Inverse)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

Find the inverse of \( f(x)=2x+1 \).

Let \( y=2x+1 \), swap and solve:

\[ f^{-1}(x)=\tfrac{x-1}{2}. \]

label.en: Worked Example C — Functions: Modulus & Inverse (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): A piecewise function is defined by \( p(t) = 4t + 2 \) for \( t < 10 \) and \( p(t) = t^2 + q \) for \( t \ge 10 \). Find the parameter \( q \) that makes \( p(t) \) continuous at \( t = 10 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Continuity at \( t = 10 \) requires \( 4(10) + 2 = 10^2 + q \implies q = -58 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Functions: Modulus & Inverse (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Given \( f(x)=-2x+4 \), find \( f^{-1}(-8) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: \( f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-4}{-2} \), so \( f^{-1}(-8)=6 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Functions: Modulus & Inverse)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+6} = x - 1\) without checking \(x - 1 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 1\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

body.en: Fast Exam Check (Cambridge International A Level (9709 Paper 3 / Paper 6)): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Modulus Inequalities & Extraneous Solutions

body.en:
Squaring Both Sides: When solving an inequality with moduli on both sides, such as \(|ax+b| < |cx+d|\), squaring both sides is fully valid because both quantities are non-negative: \((ax+b)^2 < (cx+d)^2\). This quickly reduces to a standard quadratic inequality.

Single Modulus Pitfall: Do NOT square both sides if one side can be negative (e.g. \(|2x-1| > x - 3\)). Squaring can introduce extraneous solutions or flip inequality signs unpredictably. Instead, sketch the linear graphs or split into two linear cases: \(2x-1 > x-3\) and \(2x-1 < -(x-3)\).

solution.en:
Since both sides are non-negative, square both sides:

\[(3x - 2)^2 < (x + 6)^2\]\[9x^2 - 12x + 4 < x^2 + 12x + 36\]\[8x^2 - 24x - 32 < 0\]\[x^2 - 3x - 4 < 0\]

Factor the quadratic:

\[(x - 4)(x + 1) < 0\]

The solution set is the interval between the roots:

\[-1 < x < 4\]
